translationRepairs: s0093 Chinese 〈（即遮塵。）〉 is a parenthetical gloss; the idiomatic before drops the opening parenthesis and retains a trailing corner bracket 〉. The proposed English restores a clean gloss.
The same annotation in s0093 leaves a corrupted 〉 on the literal; removing that closer while keeping “(that is, dust covers.)” matches the Chinese parenthetical.
s0208 〈（或黃線羅。）〉 is a variant parenthetical; the idiomatic before lacks the opening parenthesis, omits the period, and keeps 〉. The proposed “(or yellow cord gauze.)” restores the gloss.
The literal narrates “close bracket〉” instead of rendering 〈（或黃線羅。）〉; stripping that OCR noise to “(or yellow cord gauze.)” is correct.

In the fourth year of Longqing, when setting the suburban sacrifice completion banquet, the emperor rode a board palanquin out through the Gate of Returning to the Pole, entered through the Gate of Imperial Supremacy, and at the hall ascended and descended from the palanquin.

In the fourth year of Longqing, when setting the suburban sacrifice completion banquet, the emperor rode a board palanquin out through the Gate of Returning to the Pole, entered through the Gate of Imperial Supremacy, and at the hall descended from the palanquin.
s0176 ends 至殿上降輿 with only dismounting; unlike s0175’s 降輿升輅, there is no ascent. Removing invented “ascended and” restores the Chinese.
Commandery princesses and their daughters used di palanquins built like imperial consorts' phoenix palanquins, but with pheasants in place of phoenixes.
Commandery princes' consorts and commandery ladies used di palanquins built like imperial consorts' phoenix palanquins, but with pheasants in place of phoenixes.
郡王妃及郡主 are consorts of commandery princes and commandery ladies, not “princesses and their daughters”; the proposed idiomatic matches the titles and the unit’s own literal.

First year of Yongle, imperial son-in-law Commandant Hu Guan exceeded regulations by riding Prince Ji Xi of Jin's red open bracket carriage unit close bracket brown palanquin, and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Jing.
First year of Yongle, imperial son-in-law Commandant Hu Guan exceeded regulations by riding Prince Ji Xi of Jin's red-framed brown palanquin, and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Jing.

s0332’s 朱<車尞> is the decomposed form of 轑; CText Mingshi 輿服一 reads 朱轑棕轎, not 朱轓. Drop the OCR bracket narration, but do not invent “red-fendered”; “red-framed brown palanquin” matches the attested 朱轑.
Extraordinary exceptions did occur: during Xuande Junior Guardian Huang Huai once rode a shoulder litter into the forbidden precinct while touring the Western Park.
Extraordinary exceptions did occur: during Xuande, Junior Guardian Huang Huai once rode a shoulder litter into the forbidden precinct while touring the Western Park.
宣德中少保黃淮 separates the Xuande period from the office 少保; without a comma, “Xuande Junior Guardian” fuses the reign into the title. The proposed comma restores that boundary.
Twenty-sixth year fixed: dukes, marquises, ranks one and two used silver, iron fittings; open bracket ge zhan close bracket used silver tracery.
Twenty-sixth year fixed: dukes, marquises, ranks one and two used silver, iron fittings; saddle flaps used silver tracery.
s0363’s <革佔> is unreadable OCR; CText restores 䩞用描銀 (saddle ornament/flap). Replacing the bracket gloss with “saddle flaps” is accurate English even though the proposal mislabels the glyph as 韂.
Ranks three through five used silver, iron fittings; open bracket ge zhan close bracket used oil painting.
Ranks three through five used silver, iron fittings; saddle flaps used oil painting.
Parallel <革佔> in s0364 is likewise 䩞 in CText (䩞用油畫); “saddle flaps used oil painting” correctly replaces the OCR bracket narration.
Ranks six through nine used pewter plating, iron fittings; open bracket ge zhan close bracket used oil painting.
Ranks six through nine used pewter plating, iron fittings; saddle flaps used oil painting.
s0365 repeats the same corrupt <革佔>; CText’s 䩞用油畫 supports “saddle flaps used oil painting” over the bracket gloss.
Military and commoners used iron fittings, black-green oiled open bracket ge zhan close bracket.
Military and commoners used iron fittings, black-green oiled saddle flaps.
s0367’s 黑綠油<革佔> is 黑綠油䩞 in CText; “black-green oiled saddle flaps” removes the OCR narration without changing the fittings sense.
